name: Sandeep Engineer
forbes_bio: Chemical engineer Sandeep Engineer, started out working in the pharma industry before launching his own pharma venture in 1987.
A decade later, he began producing plastic pipes through Astral, convincing India's plumbers of their superiority over metal pipes.
Astral?s business division Astral Pipes enlists popular actors as its brand ambassadors.
The Ahmedabad firm also makes adhesives and sealants.

name: Alfons Doblinger
forbes_bio: Alfons Doblinger is the founder and controlling shareholder of German real estate developer, Doblinger Gruppe.
Doblinger started the Munich-based business in 1962 at age 17.
The group, which designs, builds and manages properties, has more than 600 employees and annual revenue of about 600 million euros.

name: Gregory Bentley
sec_insider_companies: BENTLEY SYSTEMS INC (BSY) - Executive Chair & President
forbes_bio: Gregory Bentley is chairman of infrastructure engineering software developer Bentley Systems. He was CEO from 2000 to 2024.
He joined the company in 1991 after selling a financial trading company he co-founded with brother Barry for $50 million.
His younger brothers Barry and Keith founded the software company in 1984.
Bentley Systems develops and sells computer-aided design (CAD) software for architects and engineers working on public and industrial infrastructure.
The $1.5 billion (sales) company remains majority owned by the Bentley family.
forbes_facts: Before starting their software ventures, the brothers sold Christmas trees to earn extra cash.
After the Space Shuttle Challenger exploded in 1986, NASA used Bentley Systems? software to create 3D models of the launch to help analyze what went wrong.

name: Satya Nadella
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun India (2019); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Satya Nadella joined Microsoft in 1992 and rose to CEO in 2014, when his billionaire predecessor, Steve Ballmer, retired that year.
Nadella was named chairman in 2021, replacing veteran tech exec and investor John Thompson, who had assumed the role from Microsoft's billionaire cofounder Bill Gates in 2014.
As CEO, Nadella has built Microsoft Azure into a leading cloud computing platform and overseen the acquisitions of LinkedIn for $26 billion in 2016 and Activision Blizzard for $69 billion 2023.
He has also made Microsoft a major player in the AI boom, investing billions in OpenAI since 2019 and leading the development of Microsoft's own suite of AI-powered tools called CoPilot.
He owns just 0.01% of the company's stock, but that's enough to make him a billionaire, when combined with his more than $700 million of share sales.
A native of India, Nadella came to the U.S. as a student, earning a master's in computer science from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and an MBA from the University of Chicago.

name: Tong Yongsheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun China (2017-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Tong Yongsheng leads Shenzhen Megmeet Electrica, which specializes in energy conversion technologies.
The company is a renowned domestic supplier across multiple sectors, including smart home appliances, power supply products, green energy and rail transit components.
In 2024, the company announced that it participated in the designing of NVIDIA's Blackwell system, making it one of NVIDIA's more than 40 equipment suppliers that serve its data centers.
The company has set up R&D centers in the U.S. and Germany, and plans to build manufacturing plants in Thailand, India and the U.S.
Tong Yongsheng holds Postdoctoral Fellow in Power Electronics at Zhejiang University. He worked for Huawei from 1996 to 2001 and Emerson later.
Tong assumed leadership of Megmeet in 2005 amid financial losses and has since served as chairman and CEO; the company has been profitable under his helm.

name: Joachim Goldbeck
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Joachim Goldbeck derives his fortune from the eponymous construction company founded by his father, Ortwin Goldbeck, in 1969.
His two brothers are co-CEOs of the German builder, which has 12,500 employees and 100 locations worldwide.
One of its country's largest developers, Goldbeck completes more than 500 projects annually; its services include factories, warehouses, offices, schools, parking lots and residential buildings.
He and his brothers each own about a third of the company.

name: Zhang Liguo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhang Liguo is the founder and chairman of Harbin Fuerjia Technology, a maker of skincare products best known for its beauty masks.
He took Fuerjia public in Shenzhen in August 2023, raising $306 million.
Zhang worked as a pharmacist in a local hospital before striking out on his own.

name: Keiko Erikawa
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Keiko Erikawa cofounded videogame developer Koei in 1978 with her husband Yoichi Erikawa.
The company, now called Koei Tecmo Holdings, trades on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The founders are stepping away from executive roles. Starting April, Yoichi, who is now CEO, will become chairman; and Keiko, who is now chairman, will become chairman emeritus.
The company is known for its Samurai Warrior games.
In 2021, Keiko Erikawa was appointed as an independent director of SoftBank Group. She's the only woman to sit on the company's board.

name: David Humphreys
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: David Humphreys is an heir to the Galena, Kansas-based Tamko roofing fortune.
His grandfather E. L. Craig started the company in 1944 at the age of 69 in an old streetcar barn in Joplin, Missouri.
Today, Tamko is the fourth-largest manufacturer of roofing shingles in the United States. The company recorded $1.2 billion in 2023 revenue.
David took over as president and CEO of Tamko in 1994 after his father's death; he and his wife Debra both serve on Tamko's board of directors.
The Humphreys family sold a 25% stake in the business to the Carlyle Group, a $447 billion (assets under management) private equity firm, for an undisclosed sum in 2019.
David and his sister Sarah, and their respective families, split the remaining 75%.
forbes_facts: A libertarian who has given millions to Missouri Republicans, David Humphreys has also been an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump.
Humphreys' passions include tennis, rare books and history.
